data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004 declares separation unnecessary because execution is the only valid verification, but its own countercondition concedes a circular dependency if the same engine authors the test code. This admits that engine identity can poison verification, contradicting the blanket claim that separation is a red herring. The problem explicitly asks whether separating authoring from checking is necessary; SRC_004's own exception shows separation (at least of test authorship) is necessary in the common computable case, so its core claim is self-undermined.
